decisions.reason: A traditional rye country bread fits the firm's core handcraft identity and has its own product page, so the low-cost line is likely to persist.
The premium raisin stollen won the German Bread Institute gold medal again and is publicly promoted, making it a flagship the firm will keep.
The seeded rye mixed bread builds on established recipes and production, so continuing it costs little and confirms the firm's traditional bread direction.
The dark malt rye bread is a niche variant, but it is visibly listed and fits the regional bread range, so any weak sales would likely be put down to temporary causes.
The marzipan stollen belongs to the firm's central seasonal gift assortment alongside the award-winning stollen, which strongly favors keeping it.
The ancient grain bread is a slightly trendier addition with no reported results, but its public presentation and its fit with the quality positioning argue for persisting with it.
